svg.title: Reliability for agent memory: provenance, forgetting, and trust audits
svg.desc: Poster version 4. Left column: the silent propagation failure and a dot vote on forget semantics. Centre column: the confidence chain and the erasure inflation paradox as the hero panel. Right column: the layer stack and a conformance matrix split by forget mode. Footer: a single QR to the repository.
svg.text: Reliability for agent memory: provenance, forgetting, and trust audits
What breaks when agents share memory — and how to test for it
and acts on it as fact
no signal · no chain · nothing to audit
Storage answers what the agent saw.
It never answers how much to believe it.
one dot each · board photographed at 8pm · results go in the repo
2 · Confidence is bounded by the chain
a claim cannot outscore its weakest ancestor
3 · Then someone asks you to forget
an empty chain imposes no bound
Forgetting the evidence strengthens the conclusion.
Tombstones hide this. Real erasure exposes it. Same test, one flag.
Open questions — come argue with me
Should min over an empty chain be 1.0, 0.0, or a refusal to answer?
Source forgotten, derivative still correct. Now what?
Should an exception seen twice ever become a rule?
→ cast a dot on the forget question, bottom left
same suite, same assertion, one configuration flag
grades are generated by the harness, not asserted by me
spec · failure taxonomy · conformance suite · reproduce with one command · Apache 2.0
